idiom_name: Typed Express route handler per page, or NestJS @Get action method
implementation_notes: The page controller is a route handler whose types encode the page contract: Express' @types/express infers req.params from the route path (reading a name that is not in the path is a compile error), Request<Params, ResBody, ReqBody, ReqQuery> documents the page's inputs when the handler is defined away from the route, and res.render selects the view - the callback is the controller, with middleware carrying shared behaviour. NestJS is the structured sibling: one @Controller('orders') class per page area, one @Get()/@Post() method per page, dependency injection and interceptors replacing the base controller. Prefer the typed-handler form for page-scoped services and NestJS when the application needs modules and DI.
pitfalls: Defining the handler away from the route loses the inferred params type: annotate Request<{ id: string }> explicitly or the page contract silently degrades to any.
req.session is untyped unless you augment the session declaration, so a typo in a session key compiles and only fails at runtime.
Async handlers must forward their rejections (try/catch plus next(err), or a wrapper): in Express 4 a rejected promise never reaches the error middleware.
